text: Gentlemen. This week the lab boys taught the robot the hardest word in the English language. Stop.

On the left, last week's model. We said stop. It kept hitting the obsidian for nine more seconds. On the right, this week's. One stop, the swing ends, it lets go of the keys, and the obsidian survives. The obsidian sent us a thank-you note. We framed it.
Six stops out of six. And it still walks, crafts, climbs stairs, breaks walls and bridges gaps. Forty-two courses, forty-two passes. I asked for forty-three. Budget cuts.
Problem number two. Tell the robot, get near that lava, and it insisted on standing exactly on the spot. The spot was inside a wall. So it stared at the wall. Very loyal. Not very bright.
Now it reads the word near the way you and I do. Any safe block inside the circle will do. One step down, stand at the edge, and that is a bucket of lava. Six fresh tries, six buckets.
Is the game beaten? No. There is one more lava stall, a long one. The lab boys went in after it with flashlights. They have not come back. We are sending more lab boys.
Version zero point nine five point five eight. Out now, free, open source. Go on. Tell it to stop.
